title: Volume 2 · Quote to Cash, Step by Step
subtitle: Lessons 1–5: quotation, sales order, delivery note, sales invoice and payment, with the exact numbers each step must produce
outcomes: Walk a sale from quotation to cash without breaking the chain of references
Know exactly which document writes to the general ledger, the stock ledger and the payment ledger
Predict the tax, cost of goods sold and gross profit of a sample sale to the sen
Convert documents forward instead of retyping them, and explain why that matters
Reconcile the three ledgers after the cycle and prove the books agree

slides.title: The quotation writes nothing except an offer
bullets: A quotation is a promise, not a transaction: no ledger entries, no stock movement, no receivable
Selecting the customer brings the price list, currency and payment terms from the master
The valid-till date drives the expiry report the sales team works from
Items added here use the three-layer price resolution from Volume 1
Submitting locks the document; converting to a sales order copies it without retyping

rows: Price list Retail - SM, terms 30 days

slides.notes: Learners expect a quotation to reserve stock or create a receivable. It does neither, and saying so clearly prevents a month of confusion. The tax template can be applied at quotation level, and doing it here means the customer sees the inclusive total from the first conversation rather than discovering it on the invoice.

slides.title: Prove a quotation changed nothing
bullets: The document status reads Open and it appears in the Quotation list with a valid-till date
The general ledger has no entries referencing this quotation, because none exist
Stock Balance still shows zero for the blender, so nothing was reserved
The customer dashboard still shows zero credit exposure
The Make button offers Sales Order and, later in the flow, nothing else
slides.notes: The empty general ledger is the teaching point, and it is best shown by filtering the report on the quotation number and getting nothing back. That single action builds trust in the whole document chain: learners stop assuming that saving a document posts something. Run it before and after each conversion in the rest of the volume.

callout.title: Zero is a result
callout.text: An empty report is evidence. Show it deliberately, or the client will assume the system posted in the background.

slides.title: A commitment, with dates and warehouses on every line
bullets: The sales order is the commitment that planning, buying and delivery all read from
Delivery date and warehouse per line are what make the order schedulable
No stock moves and no ledger posts, but projected quantity drops by the ordered amount
Per-billed and per-delivered percentages control staged or partial fulfilment
Convert from the quotation so rates, terms and taxes carry across exactly

rows: Open the quotation → Make → Sales Order

slides.notes: Explain the difference between actual and projected quantity: the order reserves nothing physical, but it tells the planner that five units are promised. That distinction is what makes the stock projection report useful and why an order can exist with zero stock on hand. Per-billed and per-delivered percentages are the consultant's tool for staged billing and partial supply.

slides.title: Commitment visible, stock untouched
bullets: The order shows To Deliver and Bill and links back to the quotation it came from
Projected quantity for the item falls by five while actual stock remains zero
The Stock Balance report still reads zero in every warehouse
The order appears in the Sales Order Analysis report under the correct territory
The Make button now offers Delivery Note and Sales Invoice
slides.notes: The projected quantity is the first place a learner sees the difference between planning and movement. Use it to introduce the stock projection report, which is the single most useful screen for a sales manager. If projected quantity does not change, the order was saved as a draft rather than submitted.

callout.title: Draft orders lie
callout.text: A draft sales order reserves nothing and appears in no commitment report. Train the team to submit, or reporting will understate demand.

slides.title: Where the stock ledger finally moves
bullets: The delivery note is the physical event: stock leaves and cost of goods sold posts
Convert from the order so quantities cannot drift between promise and dispatch
With FIFO valuation, five units at 120.00 write a 600.00 cost of goods entry
The order's per-delivered percentage jumps to 100 and its status becomes To Bill
A delivery note is not an invoice: the customer has goods and no receivable yet

rows: Open the order → Make → Delivery Note

slides.notes: This is the slide where accounting meets the warehouse. Show both ledgers side by side: stock quantity leaves, and a value moves from inventory to cost of goods sold. Learners who have only used invoicing software are surprised that a delivery note posts anything at all, and that surprise is exactly why this course exists.

slides.title: Five units out, six hundred in cost
bullets: Stock Balance shows zero in Main Warehouse with no negative quantity anywhere
The Stock Ledger shows a single outgoing row of 5 at valuation 120.00
The general ledger shows a 600.00 debit to cost of goods sold and a matching credit to stock
The sales order is fully delivered and waiting to be billed
No debtors balance exists yet, which is the difference between shipping and selling
slides.notes: Ask the learner where the profit is at this moment: nowhere, because revenue has not been recognised. That is the accounting lesson behind the document split, and it is why a month can have busy dispatch and no revenue. If stock goes negative, a receipt is missing and the fix is the receipt, never the report.

callout.title: Negative stock after a delivery
callout.text: It means the goods were never received in the system. Post the purchase receipt with the correct date, then check the stock ledger again.

slides.title: Revenue, receivable and tax in one posting
bullets: Convert from the delivery note so billed quantity equals dispatched quantity
Submitting posts three things: revenue, a receivable and a tax liability
The payment ledger now shows 1,320.00 outstanding against this invoice
The sales order completes because per-billed reaches 100 per cent
Revenue 1,200.00 less cost 600.00 gives gross profit 600.00, a fifty per cent margin

rows: Open the delivery note → Make → Sales Invoice
Customer sees net, tax and total

slides.notes: Ask for the three postings before pressing submit: who owes, what revenue, and what tax. This is the sentence a consultant says in every user training session, and getting a client's accounts team to recite it is worth more than any slide. Emphasise converting rather than retyping so the quantities match to the unit.

slides.title: The four numbers that must be exact
bullets: Debtors increases by 1,320.00 and the invoice appears in aged receivables
Sales revenue is 1,200.00 and SST Payable is 120.00, both as credits
Cost of goods sold is 600.00 from the earlier delivery, so gross profit is 600.00
The payment ledger shows 1,320.00 outstanding, not the net amount
The sales order status becomes Completed and drops out of the to-bill queue
slides.notes: The payment ledger figure is where trainees go wrong: they expect the net 1,200.00, but the customer owes the tax-inclusive total. Show the payment ledger next to the invoice so the difference becomes obvious. Then run the Gross Profit report, which is the report a client will ask for in week one.

callout.title: Bill what you shipped
callout.text: Converting from the delivery note guarantees the invoice matches the dispatch. Retyping invoices is how quantity mismatches ruin month-end.

slides.title: Cash in, allocated, and a customer who owes nothing
bullets: A payment entry moves cash and clears the receivable, but only if it is allocated to the invoice
The invoice status changes to Paid when the payment reference is set
Bank charges are entered as a deduction on the payment, not as a separate journal
Unallocated receipts are the most common cause of a wrong aged receivables report
The payment ledger returns to zero, which is the test that the cycle is complete
slides.notes: The allocation step is the whole lesson. A receipt with no reference clears the bank and leaves the invoice open, which produces an aged receivables report nobody trusts. Demonstrate the wrong way first: post an unallocated payment, show the invoice still unpaid, then cancel it and do it properly.

slides.title: Three ledgers that agree at the end
bullets: The sales invoice is Paid and shows zero outstanding in the payment ledger
Debtors closes at zero for this customer, so aged receivables lists nothing
Bank increases by 1,320.00 with the payment as its reference
Gross profit remains 600.00, because receiving cash does not change profit
The full cycle left four documents linked by a continuous chain of conversions
slides.notes: End the volume by running three reports in sequence: general ledger for the customer, payment ledger, and gross profit. If all three agree, the learner has understood the transaction chain rather than memorised screens. This is also the moment to introduce the idea that a reconciled month is built from many such small agreements.

callout.title: Allocate, always
callout.text: Every receipt must reference an invoice. An unallocated payment is cash in the bank and a receivable still open, which is a reconciliation problem you create yourself.

lab.title: Lab · Run the full quote-to-cash cycle with exact numbers
steps: Raise a quotation for Aeon Big: 5 × SM-BL200 at 240.00, SST 10 %, valid until 31-12-2026
Confirm the quotation shows 1,200.00 net, 120.00 tax, 1,320.00 total and no ledger entries
Convert to a Sales Order with delivery date 15-11-2026 and warehouse Main Warehouse
Confirm the order is To Deliver and Bill and that projected quantity is −5
Convert to a Delivery Note and confirm stock −5, COGS 600.00 and the order at 100 % delivered
Convert to a Sales Invoice posted 15-11-2026 and verify Dr Debtors 1,320.00, Cr Sales 1,200.00, Cr SST 120.00
Print the invoice and check the customer address, tax line and total appear correctly
Post a Payment Entry of 1,320.00 from Bank - SM allocated to the invoice
Run the aged receivables, payment ledger and gross profit reports and record all three results
lab.done: The invoice is Paid, the customer's receivable is zero, gross profit is 600.00, and you can name the ledger each of the four documents wrote to.

quiz.question: Which document first writes to the stock ledger in a normal sale?
quiz.why: Only the delivery note moves stock and posts cost of goods sold. Quotations and orders are commitments; the invoice posts revenue and the receivable.

quiz.question: A sale of 1,200.00 net with 10 % SST and a 120.00 unit cost for 5 units produces what gross profit?
quiz.why: Revenue 1,200.00 less cost of goods 5 × 120.00 = 600.00 gives gross profit 600.00. Tax is a liability, not revenue.

quiz.question: What does the payment ledger show immediately after submitting the sales invoice?
quiz.why: The customer owes the tax-inclusive total, so the payment ledger shows 1,320.00 outstanding until an allocated payment clears it.

quiz.question: A receipt was posted without allocating it to an invoice. What is the symptom?
options: The invoice remains unpaid and shows in aged receivables
quiz.why: Cash reached the bank but the receivable was never cleared, so the ageing report shows an invoice that the customer has already paid.

quiz.question: Why convert documents instead of creating each one fresh?
options: It carries quantities, rates and references forward so the chain cannot drift
quiz.why: Conversion preserves the link and the values, which is what lets ERPNext track delivered and billed percentages and keeps invoice quantities equal to dispatched quantities.

narration: Volume two is the transaction chain, and this is the heart of consultant training: five documents, three ledgers, and numbers you predict before you press submit. A quotation writes nothing but an offer. It carries the customer's price list, terms and tax, and when it is submitted the general ledger stays empty and stock does not move. A sales order is a commitment. It still posts nothing, but projected quantity falls by five, delivery dates and warehouses are set per line, and the order becomes the source for delivery and billing. The delivery note is where stock finally moves. Five units leave the main warehouse at a valuation of one hundred twenty each, so cost of goods sold is six hundred, and the order says fully delivered. Still no receivable. The sales invoice posts three things at once: debtors one thousand three hundred twenty, revenue one thousand two hundred, and SST payable one hundred twenty. Gross profit becomes six hundred, a fifty percent margin. Then the payment entry. Receive one thousand three hundred twenty into the bank, allocate it to the invoice, and the invoice turns paid and the payment ledger returns to zero. An unallocated receipt is the most common cause of a wrong aged receivables report, so always allocate. In the lab you run the whole cycle and then prove it with three reports: general ledger, payment ledger and gross profit.
